Beta4: driver preflight

Hardware tessellation becomes available after a background compilation check on the current GPU/driver. This renderer check also runs with AVFX disabled. Failure retains the fallback without rewriting presets. See the video guide.


Surface Objects and materials in beta 3

Surface Materials and Surface Objects are separate layers. The object menu contains grass, wall foliage, ferns, stones, soil clumps and fallen leaves. Each has its own submenu and master switch. These are client-side decorations without collision changes. Foliage has shape and clustering controls; stones use textures and a wide size spread; leaves can fall with separate amount, speed, wind and outdoor-only controls. Grass, ivy, ferns and stones have independent shadow strength, zero by default. Flashlight projections reuse that strength and require flashlight shadows.

Independent Surface Object submenus.

Metal response and brick relief have been improved. Individual rectangular bricks use visibility and projected-detail controls; this does not replace the existing material settings.



Beta 2 additions

AVFX starts after the map and color mode are ready and releases map-owned data on exit. Fixed hangs at map-loading boundaries, including HDR. Removed false missing-cloud-texture messages for optional shader inputs without suppressing real resource errors.

Floor and wall materials now include metal coverings; see the Advanced AVFX guide for controls and examples. Metallic Lustre is available as an Extra Quality factory preset.


1. AVFX theory

AVFX is an optional client-side layer for weather, surfaces, audio and screen reactions. It does not change server physics, damage, hitboxes or game rules.
The system has four parts: weather emitters (rain/snow/ash/dust/mist), surface receivers (water, puddles, snow, lava), reactions (footsteps, weapons, steam, splashes), and presentation (sky, audio, wet lens).
AVFX is off by default for new users. Defaults are a safe quality baseline; users enable the system through presets or manual settings.
Ultra Quality means maximum visuals with distance LOD disabled: puddles and snow should not 'build only when the player arrives'. Lower tiers may use LOD and reduce secondary effects.
Presets are cfg files under baseq2/q2pro-x/visual_presets. They can be copied and edited by advanced users; menu rows simply execute the matching cfg.


2. How to enable and test

Open the main AVFX menu: Main menu → Advanced Visual Effects
For a ready-to-use setup, open the AVFX presets and choose a profile at the quality tier you want.
For manual tuning, use the detailed child pages: weather and atmosphere, surfaces and water, sky and celestials, local FX and sound.
Use cl_avfx_info for diagnostics; use the restore-defaults row to reset.
The quick commands are listed in the cvar and command reference.

3. The basic weather presets

The basic weather profiles are listed below. The complete set of shipped presets, the custom slots and the rules for saving them are covered in the separate AVFX presets guide; the way to obtain a whole new scene with one press is in the AVFX preset generator guide.

PresetFilePurpose

Rain Ultrav_p_r_u.cfgThe same rain/water quality baseline without storm/lightning emphasis.

4. Quality tiers

TierWhat it doesWhen to use it
Ultra QualityLOD off, maximum density, large puddles/snow/surface cover, expensive secondary effects enabled.Screenshots, powerful PCs, reference visuals.
QualityClose to Ultra, with mild LOD and slightly reduced density/expensive detail.Recommended high-quality play.
BalancedMore visible LOD and lower particle density, while keeping the AVFX identity.When you want a clear FPS boost without losing the feel.
PerformanceReduces particles and some expensive secondary effects while keeping weather readable.Multiplayer or heavy maps.
Ultra PerformanceAggressive LOD and minimal extras; sounds remain enabled.Weak PCs, maximum speed, compatibility checks.

6. Profile-specific tuning

Rain and storm

Start with Rain & Storm Ultra or Rain Quality. Then tune cl_avfx_density, cl_avfx_rain_drop_density and cl_avfx_rain_puddle_fill_rate.
For rich surfaces, keep cl_avfx_rain_puddles, cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff, cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples and cl_avfx_rain_puddle_specular enabled.
If FPS drops, first enable cl_avfx_render_lod and reduce cl_avfx_render_lod_wu, then lower puddle rings, bubbles, dust and splash density.
For storm mood, key controls are cl_avfx_storm, cl_avfx_lightning, cl_avfx_lightning_frequency, cl_avfx_audio_thunder and sky cloud/fog settings.

Snow

Start with Snow Ultra. The main visuals come from cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material, cl_avfx_snow_gpu_coverage, cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d.
Accumulation speed is controlled by cl_avfx_snow_accum_fill_rate. The practical 0.01..3.00 range is used because high values fill maps almost instantly.
If 3D snowflakes are disabled, ordinary small snow should still fall; visibility depends on the general particle/weather profile.
Footprints, weapon marks and impact strength should scale with snow depth and the parallax snowdrift feel.

Competitive play

For maximum visibility use AVFX off or Performance/Ultra Performance.
Enable cl_avfx_competitive_limit if effects must not interfere with model/item readability.
Keep sounds if useful, but reduce rain-on-eyes, storm flashes, puddle rings and dense snowflakes.


7. Troubleshooting

No effects: check cl_avfx 1, cl_avfx_preset not Off, cl_avfx_world 1, multiplayer/demo gates and the actual selected cfg preset.
No AVFX audio: check cl_avfx_audio 1, cl_avfx_audio_volume, s_ambient and WAV files under baseq2/sound/q2prox/avfx.
After experiments the state looks odd: apply the desired preset again or use /avfxr.
For clean release testing, do not carry old q2pro-x.cfg/q2pro-x.local.cfg from earlier builds if you want new-user defaults.



8. Modes: multiplayer, demos and the competitive limit

AVFX Modes

TypeSectionRowVariable or targetWhat it does
ToggleMultiplayercl_avfx_multiplayerAllow AVFX during real multiplayer matches; off disables it there. Applies immediately.
ToggleDemo playbackcl_avfx_demoAllow AVFX during demo (.dm2/.mvd2) playback. Applies immediately.
ToggleCompetitive limitcl_avfx_competitive_limitIn multiplayer, caps alpha/density/particle counts so weather can't hide targets. Applies immediately.

Besides these modes there is a global AVFX disable: it switches the layer off across every mod without rewriting local settings or presets. That is convenient when you want a clean image for a while without losing a configured profile.
